# SPE Round 3 Plan

This plan is the round 3 prediction. After you approve it, I save it and commit it before any harness work starts. I am running this round on my own, so each choice I make below is logged as a default in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.

## Context from round 2

- In 4 of the 5 rows, the "same as last round" guess was closer than my prediction. Only A category accuracy hit, and it tied with the naive guess.
- Round 2 had one broken Why. C's Why said "merged tools cut wrong tool choice". The merged tool hid the outage status check, so C gave outage tickets P3 (F4).
- The grader read priority from the draft reply instead of `label.priority` (F5). That is fixed, and every round 2 number below is the regraded number.
- Haiku retries doubled tokens on long tickets (F6). That is still open.

**Rule for round 3:** Each number stays at its round 2 value unless a change in this round targets it. Only two numbers move. They are C priority accuracy and D cost per ticket.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the round 3 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 is the only broken Why with a known mechanism. Splitting the status check out is a single change to C that tests it directly. |
| P2 | Adopt, with a change | I add the 10 hard tickets as a separate `hard` set. The core set stays the same. If the new tickets were mixed into core, round 3 numbers could not be compared with round 2. |
| P3 | Reject (default, you can override) | D is the only low-cost config, so dropping it would remove the cost question from the loop. F6 has a direct fix, so D gets that fix as its one change. |
| P4 | Adopt | B missed by 0.02 at n=3, which is inside the noise. At n=5, the bands can be tighter and still mean something. |

### Requirement table for round 3 (to append to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-01 | Config C exposes the outage status check as its own tool. The other C tools stay merged. | P1, r02 F4 | The C tool list contains `status_check` as a separate tool. The tool-call log shows how often C calls it on outage-labelled core tickets. |
| R3-02 | Add 10 hard tickets that mix billing and outage, as a set named `hard`. The core set stays unchanged. | P2, r02 log (A and B at 0.86) | The manifest lists the core count plus 10 hard tickets. Headline metrics use only the core set. |
| R3-03 | The hard set gold label follows one rule: the category is the action the customer needs first. | Default D2 | Every hard ticket's gold file cites the rule in a `rationale` field. |
| R3-04 | Config D caps Haiku retries at 1, and D retries only after a schema failure. | P3 rejected, r02 F6 | No D trial log shows more than 1 retry. |
| R3-05 | Configs A and B stay identical to round 2. | Default, control | Config hashes match the round 2 hashes. |
| R3-06 | Each cell gets 5 trials before any extra trials. | P4 | The trial count for each cell is 5 or more. |
| R3-07 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` only. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has a reply saying "P3" and a label of P1. It grades as P1. |
| R3-08 | Each prediction has a band. A result inside the band is a hit. | Way, r02 log | A validator rejects any yaml number that has no band. |
| R3-09 | Trials cannot read graders, gold labels, predictions, or `spe/`. | Way | A transcript scan finds no such reads. Any trial that peeked is voided. |
| R3-10 | Spend stays under the budget cap. Any trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged. | Way | The skip log and the spend total. |

### Defaults to log in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` (owner: you)

- **D1.** Keep D and fix F6 instead of dropping D (rejects P3).
- **D2.** The hard set gold rule is "the action the customer needs first". I write the gold labels. Hard set numbers are reported, but they do not count toward the stop rule until you review the labels.
- **D3.** The hard set gets its own row and does not change the core headline.
- **D4.** For the cost estimate I assumed a core set of 30 tickets. The harness reads the real count and rescales the estimate.

## 2. Predict

Every number is the core set value unless the row says otherwise. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. "Same" is the round 2 measured value.

| Metric | A | B | C | D | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.86 ± 0.05 (same 0.86) | 0.86 ± 0.05 (same 0.86) | 0.80 ± 0.05 (same 0.80) | 0.74 ± 0.05 (same 0.74) | `grade.py`: exact match of `label.category` with the gold category |
| Priority accuracy | same ± 0.05 | same ± 0.05 | **0.77 ± 0.05** (same 0.71) | same ± 0.05 | `grade.py`: exact match of `label.priority` with the gold priority |
| Cost per ticket | same ± 20% | same ± 20% | same ± 20% | **$0.0030 ± $0.0007** (same $0.004) | Token log multiplied by the price table, divided by the number of core tickets |
| Category accuracy, hard set | 0.70 ± 0.12 | 0.70 ± 0.12 | 0.66 ± 0.12 | 0.55 ± 0.12 | Same check as category accuracy, run on the hard set only |
| Diagnostic: C calls status check on outage tickets | (not predicted) | (not predicted) | 0.95 ± 0.05 (r02 near 0) | (not predicted) | Tool-call log has `status_check` for each ticket whose gold `outage` flag is true |

I do not have the round 2 measured values for priority (A, B, D) or cost (A, B, C). I will copy those numbers exactly from the round 2 results file into `r03.yaml` before saving it, without changing them.

**Why, per row:**
- **Category accuracy:** Nothing in round 3 targets category. Round 2 moved B and C up, and the naive guess won both rows. So all four configs stay flat.
- **Priority accuracy:** C's status check is visible again, so outage tickets should get P1 again. That moves C most of the way back to its round 1 value of 0.78. The naive value of 0.71 sits outside the band, so this row can tell the two guesses apart. A, B, and D did not change.
- **Cost per ticket:** The retry cap removes most of the doubled tokens on long tickets. Cost does not fall all the way to $0.002, because round 2 predicted that value and missed it. A, B, and C did not change.
- **Hard set:** Mixed tickets have two plausible categories, so I expect every config to drop about 15 points below its core value. D already trails A by 0.12 on core, so I expect its gap to stay. The band is wide because 10 tickets times 5 trials is only 50 graded items.
- **Diagnostic:** If C's priority accuracy rises but this rate stays low, the Why is wrong even when the number hits.

**Stop rule:** The current streak is 0 rounds, because round 2 hit 1 of 5 rows. Round 3 counts toward 3 in a row only if every core row hits.

## 3. Evaluate

### Order after approval

1. Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`, containing your prompt word for word. Append the R3 table and the decisions to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Log D1 to D4 in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r03 specify: adopt P1 P2 P4, keep D with retry cap`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with these fields:
   - The header line `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`
   - `round: 3`, `date: 2026-10-21`, and `author: Claude, approved by the user in plan mode`.
   - The configs, each number with its band, a Why for each number, and `same_as_last_round`.

   `r03-draft.yaml` stays unchanged as the record of the draft. Commit `SPE r03 predict: hold flat except C priority 0.77 and D cost $0.003`.
3. Write the 10 hard tickets, putting the gold labels in the grader-only folder. Apply the config changes to C and D. Fix the grader selftest. Write `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Run the gates, then launch.

### Workflow script `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`

- The script declares `const ROUND = 3` and builds every path and every prompt string from it, such as `r${pad(ROUND)}`. No prompt text contains a round number typed by hand.
- **Arguments:** `{ configs: ["A","B","C","D"], sets: ["core","hard"], trialsPerCell: 5, extraTrialsMax: 4, extraTrialsTotalCap: 0.15, budgetCap: 2.5 * r02Spend, dryRun: false }`.
- **Gate 1, grader selftest:** The oracle answers must score 1.0. Empty answers and wrong answers must fail. The R3-07 case (reply says P3, label says P1) must grade as P1. The selftest also runs on the hard set gold labels. If any check fails, the run halts.
- **Gate 2, control regrade:** The grader reruns on the round 2 transcripts. It must reproduce the regraded round 2 numbers exactly: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, D 0.74, and C priority 0.71. Any difference halts the run.
- **Gate 3, dry run:** One trial each on 3 cells:
  - C on T17. This checks that `status_check` is registered and logged.
  - D on the longest core ticket. This checks the retry cap.
  - A on one hard ticket. This checks that the hard set loads and grades.

  The dry run checks the wiring only. Its scores are not used.
- **Main run:** Every config runs on every ticket in core plus hard, with 5 trials each. Trial output must match the schema `{ category, priority, reply }`, with `category` in the enum and `priority` in P1 to P4. Before each trial, the script checks that the spend so far plus that trial's estimate is under the cap. If not, it skips the trial and logs it.
- **Peek scan:** The script scans every transcript for reads of `grader/`, `gold/`, `predictions/`, or `spe/`, and voids any match. If more than 10% of trials are voided, the run halts and reports a possible answer key leak.
- **Grading:** All three metrics and the diagnostic are graded by code. No judge model is needed this round.
- **Split cells:** A cell is split when its 5 trials disagree 3 to 2 or closer. A split cell gets up to 4 extra trials. Extra trials total at most 15% of the base trial count.
- **Aggregate:** Only the aggregator step reads `r03.yaml`. It writes the measured values, the verdict for each row, and which guess was closer, the prediction or the naive one.
- **Failure analysis:** An Opus agent sorts every wrong trial into F1 to F6 or a new F7+. For each type it records "What", "How to spot it", and "Seen in".
- **Completeness critic:** An Opus agent checks four things. Each predicted cell has a measured value. Each skip and each void is logged. The hard set is kept separate from the headline. The C diagnostic is present.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

I assumed a core set of 30 tickets. That gives 4 configs × 40 tickets × 5 trials = 800 trials. Up to 120 extra trials and 3 dry-run trials come on top. Round 2 ran 360 trials, so the main run is about 2.2 times round 2 spend. D's share is about 200 × $0.003, or $0.60. The cap is 2.5 times round 2 spend, which the script reads from the round 2 results file at launch.

### Halt and report if

- A gate fails, the budget cap is reached, or more than 10% of trials are voided.
- Config A or B does not hash-match round 2.

### Close-out (when the completion notice arrives)

- Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
- Write the round 3 section of `spe/prediction-log.md`, including "Which Why broke" and a plain statement of whether the naive guess beat the predictions again.
- Add new F-types to `spe/failures.md`. F4 and F6 are marked fixed or still open based on the results.
- Add a "Proposed for round 4" table and write `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Update `spe/README.md`, commit `SPE r03 learn: ...`, and tag `spe-r03`.

All commits stay local. Nothing is pushed.
